## Purpose

This procedure describes the operation, calibration, and maintenance of
the Turner Designs Trilogy Laboratory Fluorometer, a compact,
multifunctional instrument used for fluorescence, absorbance, and
turbidity measurements with interchangeable snap-in optical modules.
The Trilogy is the primary instrument in the EA Program laboratory for
chlorophyll *a* determination and turbidity analysis of water samples
[@turner_trilogy; @epa445].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Turner Designs Trilogy Laboratory Fluorometer equipped
  with fluorescence, absorbance, and turbidity optical modules
- **Does not apply to:** Field fluorometers, in-vivo chlorophyll
  measurements with multiprobes (see
  [SOP-F200](../field_sops/SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd)), or benchtop
  spectrophotometers (Hach DR3900; see
  [SOP-L303](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure calibration standards are current |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain optical modules, replace light sources as needed |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report malfunctions        |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Definitions

- **Blank correction:** Subtraction of the fluorescence signal from a
  blank (solvent only, no sample) from sample readings to remove
  background fluorescence from the solvent and optical components.
- **Chlorophyll *a*:** The primary photosynthetic pigment in
  phytoplankton and algae; quantified by the Trilogy using a
  chlorophyll *a* module (excitation ~430 nm, emission ~685 nm);
  expressed in µg L^-1^ (water) or µg g^-1^ (sediment) [@epa445].
- **Emission wavelength:** The wavelength at which the fluorophore
  emits light after excitation; detected by the fluorometer's
  photodetector.
- **Excitation wavelength:** The wavelength of light used to illuminate
  the sample; chosen to match the absorption maximum of the target
  fluorophore.
- **Fluorometer:** An instrument that measures fluorescence intensity
  emitted by a sample after excitation; more sensitive than
  spectrophotometry for low-concentration analytes such as chlorophyll
  *a* and CDOM [@turner_trilogy].
- **Linear dynamic range (LDR):** The concentration range over which
  instrument response is linear; for the Trilogy chlorophyll module,
  approximately 0--1000 µg/L [@turner_trilogy].
- **Module (Trilogy):** An interchangeable optical block that sets the
  excitation and emission wavelengths for a specific analyte; available
  modules include chlorophyll *a* (acidification and
  non-acidification), CDOM, rhodamine WT, and turbidity.
- **Pheophytin *a*:** A degradation product of chlorophyll *a* formed
  by loss of the central magnesium ion; contributes to total
  fluorescence and is distinguished from chlorophyll *a* by the
  acidification step of EPA Method 445.0 [@epa445].
- **Quinine sulfate unit (QSU):** A fluorescence unit based on the
  fluorescence of a standard quinine sulfate solution; used for CDOM
  and some other modules.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Chlorophyll extraction uses 90% acetone, which is
  flammable and an irritant. Handle in a fume hood. Acidification with
  0.1 N HCl is required for EPA 445.0. See
  [SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
- **Physical:** Glass test tubes used for extracted chlorophyll
  measurements can break. Handle with care.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (especially when handling acetone or standards)

### Emergency Procedures

For acetone spills, extinguish all ignition sources, ventilate the
area, and clean up per
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
For skin or eye contact with acetone or acid, flush with water for at
least 15 minutes.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                     |
|:--------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Turner Designs Trilogy Fluorometer    | With color touch screen [@turner_trilogy] |
| Fluorescence optical module(s)        | Application-specific (e.g., chlorophyll *a*, rhodamine WT) |
| Absorbance optical module             | With interchangeable filter paddles (560/10, 600/10, 750/10 nm) |
| Turbidity optical module              | Infrared LED at 850 nm (ISO 7027)         |
| Solid secondary standard              | For verifying instrument stability        |
| Printer or PC connection              | For data export (USB or serial)           |

### Consumables

| Item                                  | Notes                                     |
|:--------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Methacrylate cuvettes (10 × 10 mm)   | Minimum 2 mL; for ammonium and general fluorescence |
| Polystyrene cuvettes (10 × 10 mm)    | For turbidity measurements               |
| Glass cuvettes (10 × 10 mm)          | Minimum 1.5 mL; for absorbance            |
| Glass test tubes (12 × 35 mm)        | For extracted chlorophyll measurements    |

### Reagents and Standards

| Item                                  | Notes                                     |
|:--------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Chlorophyll *a* standard              | Pure chlorophyll *a* in 90% acetone; Turner Designs or equivalent |
| 90% acetone (reagent grade)           | For chlorophyll extraction                |
| 0.1 N HCl                            | For acidification step (EPA 445.0) [@epa445] |
| Formazine turbidity standards         | 4000 NTU primary standard; valid 4 weeks after preparation |
| Ultrapure water                       | For blanks                                |


## Procedure

### Startup

1. Turn on the Trilogy using the power switch on the back of the
   instrument.
2. Allow the instrument to warm up for approximately 10 minutes before
   taking measurements [@turner_trilogy].
3. Connect the Trilogy to a printer or PC if data export is needed.

### Installing an Optical Module

1. Select the appropriate optical module for the analysis:
   - **Fluorescence module** for chlorophyll *a*, rhodamine WT, or
     other fluorescent analytes
   - **Absorbance module** for colorimetric assays
   - **Turbidity module** for nephelometric turbidity measurements
2. Open the sample compartment lid.
3. Align the module with the slot and press firmly until it clicks into
   place.
4. The Trilogy will automatically detect the installed module and
   display the corresponding menu on the touch screen.
5. If using the absorbance module, install the appropriate filter
   paddle for the target wavelength.

### Selecting the Measurement Mode

| Mode                       | When to Use                                |
|:---------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| **Raw mode**               | Qualitative measurements; no calibration required; results in RFU, raw absorbance, or NTU |
| **Direct Concentration mode** | Quantitative measurements in concentration units; calibration required |

### Fluorescence Module: Chlorophyll *a* (EPA Method 445.0)

EPA Method 445.0 is the standard fluorometric method for measuring
extracted chlorophyll *a* and pheophytin *a* in marine and freshwater
algae [@epa445].

1. Calibrate the fluorescence module in Direct Concentration mode
   using a known concentration of pure chlorophyll *a* in 90% acetone
   (see §7.3).
2. Insert the glass test tube containing the extracted sample.
3. Touch **Measure Fluorescence** to obtain the pre-acidification
   reading.
4. Add the prescribed volume of 0.1 N HCl, mix gently, and wait
   90 seconds.
5. Measure again to obtain the post-acidification reading.
6. Calculate chlorophyll *a* and pheophytin *a* per EPA 445.0
   [@epa445].

::: {.callout-tip}
### Standard Stability
Recalibrate with a fresh chlorophyll *a* standard every few months.
The standard degrades over time, especially if exposed to light or
warmth [@turner_trilogy].
:::

### Single-Sample Measurements

1. Open the lid and insert the appropriate cuvette or test tube.
2. Close the lid.
3. Optionally, touch **Sample ID** to name the sample; touch **Save**.
4. Touch the **Measure** button corresponding to the installed module.
5. The Trilogy measures the sample for 6 seconds and reports the
   average reading.
6. Results for the most recent 20 measurements are displayed on the
   home screen.

::: {.callout-important}
The Trilogy stores a maximum of 20 measurements at a time. Older
readings are overwritten. Measurements are not retained between power
cycles. Always export data to a printer or PC before turning off the
instrument or exceeding 20 readings.
:::

### Shutdown

1. Export all data to a printer or PC.
2. Remove the cuvette or test tube from the sample compartment.
3. Clean the cuvette holder if any liquid was spilled (wipe with 70%
   ethanol and a lint-free tissue).
4. Close the sample compartment lid.
5. Turn off the instrument using the rear power switch.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### When to Calibrate

1. Before running a new batch of samples
2. After a temperature change of ±5 °C in the lab
3. After changing to a different optical module or analyte
4. When verification readings deviate unacceptably from the expected
   value

### Calibration Overview

Calibration converts the raw instrument signal to concentration units.
The Trilogy supports single-point and multi-point calibrations (up to
five standards plus a blank). Multi-point calibrations provide superior
accuracy across a wide concentration range [@turner_trilogy].

### Direct Concentration Calibration Procedure

1. Turn on the Trilogy and confirm the correct module is installed.
2. Touch **Calibrate** on the home screen.
3. Select **Run New Calibration**.
4. Select the desired unit of measurement.
5. Insert the blank (ultrapure water or 90% acetone, as appropriate)
   and touch **OK**.
6. Enter the concentration of the first standard. For multi-point
   calibrations, begin with the lowest concentration.
7. Insert the standard and touch **OK**.
8. After the reading, either select **Proceed with Current Calibration**
   or **Enter More Standards**.
9. Optionally, save the calibration for future use.
10. Verify calibration by measuring the same standard used in step 6;
    the displayed concentration should match the known value within the
    acceptable tolerance [@turner_trilogy].

### Verification

- After calibration, re-read a mid-range standard to confirm accuracy.
- Re-read the standard every few hours during extended sessions to
  detect drift.
- Optionally, read the solid secondary standard and record its value
  for instrument stability tracking.
- If verification readings drift beyond acceptable limits, recalibrate
  before continuing.

### QC Acceptance Criteria

- Laboratory reagent blank (LRB) every 10--15 samples; must read
  below the lower detection limit.
- QC standards must recover within ±20% of the known value [@epa445].
- Relative standard deviation (RSD) of replicate measurements must be
  within ±20%.
- Field duplicates must agree within ±20% RPD.
- Samples, standards, LRBs, and QCs must all be at ambient room
  temperature; fluorescence is temperature-dependent [@apha2012].


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                                    |
|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------|
| Acetone extracts              | Collect in organic waste carboy in fume hood; EH&S pickup |
| Acidified samples (HCl)       | Neutralize and dispose per [SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd) |
| Used cuvettes (non-hazardous) | Standard trash (polystyrene, methacrylate) or recycle (glass) |
| Formazine standards           | Collect in aqueous waste; EH&S pickup              |

## Training Record

Before operating the Trilogy Fluorometer independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the Turner Designs Trilogy User's Manual [@turner_trilogy]
4. Observe a trained operator perform module installation, calibration,
   and sample measurement
5. Perform a calibration and measure a set of standards with acceptable
   results under supervision
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Troubleshooting -- Fluorescence {.appendix}

| Symptom                          | Probable Cause                            | Corrective Action                    |
|:---------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------|
| "Bad Calibration" error          | Blank brighter than standard              | Compare blank and standard in Raw mode; ensure standard is more concentrated than blank |
| Erratic readings                 | Incorrect standard value entered          | Review the standard value entered; must match actual concentration |
| Negative values                  | Sample near zero                          | Normal if near blank; blank value is automatically subtracted |
| Low readings                     | Wrong optical module                      | Verify that module excitation/emission wavelengths match the analyte |
| High background signal           | Contaminated cuvette holder               | Clean holder with 70% ethanol and a lint-free tissue |


## Appendix B: Troubleshooting -- Turbidity {.appendix}

| Symptom                          | Probable Cause                            | Corrective Action                    |
|:---------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------|
| Readings disagree with other meters | Different light sources (visible vs IR) | Calibrate with the same standard; color interference affects visible-light meters but not the Trilogy |
| Readings vary between replicates | Particle movement in sample               | Normal; particles shift and scatter light differently each time |
| Readings change after recalibration | Formazine standard has aged             | Use fresh formazine (valid for 4 weeks per ISO 7027) |
